THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 10.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.2428/2018  3  2025:KER:11447  JUDGMENT Dated this the 10th day of February, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.756/2016 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thaliparamba is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 24.8.2015.
During the pendency of the appeal, the original petitioner died and the legal representatives were impleaded as additional appellants 2 to 4.

According to the petitioner, on 24.8.2015 at about 3 p.m.,
while he was walking through the side of the road near old bus stand at Payyannur, a bus bearing registration No. KL 59L 1215 in a rash and negligent manner, hit him and as a result of which he sustained serious injuries.

The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:11447 offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.23,29,000/- (limited to Rs.23,00,000/-).
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A8, B1, and X1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,19,100/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. M.V. Ameresan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri. P.
Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the petitioner was engaged as concrete worker,
earning Rs.1200/- per day, but the Tribunal fixed his notional income at Rs.6,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2015 will come to Rs.10,000/-.

sentences.text:
Since the petitioner could not prove his job or income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa (supra) , his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.10,000/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:

2025:KER:11447 13.
Exhibit X1 disability certificate shows that the petitioner suffered 52% permanent physical disability.

However, the learned counsel for the petitioners would argue that the right leg above the knee and four toes of the left leg of the petitioner were amputated and as such he was unable to do any job or earn anything and hence his functional disability is to be fixed at 100%.
The said prayer was opposed by the learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 68 years.
He claimed that he was a concrete worker at the time of accident.
In the accident he sustained very serious injuries.
Even as per the medical board, he sustained 52% permanent physical disability.

It is also revealed that his right leg above the knee and four toes of left leg were amputated and as such it is evident that he could not continue his job as a concrete worker or earn anything and as such I am inclined to fix his functional disability at 100%.
15.

Since on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 68 years, there is no scope for any future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
and the multiplier to be applied is 5, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport 2025:KER:11447 Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.6,00,000/-.
15. Since the functional disability of the petitioner is taken as 100%, he is not entitled to get any further compensation on the head 'loss of earnings'.
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs1,00,000/-.
Towards 'transport to hospital' Rs.3,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner,
the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
18. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and he was treated as inpatient for 49 days.

Considering the fact that, because of the accident his right leg above the knee and four toes of left leg were to be amputated, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.1,50,000/-.
Similarly compensation on the head 'transport to hospital' is enhanced to Rs.10,000/-.
19. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
